angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 170,447 km at 32.18 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 31.0721 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 32.18 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.245 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2120 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract): 170,447 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.211 +/- 0.005 solar masses from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2120 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3131 +/- 30 K from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2120 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hori et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2120 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2120.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.984, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2120 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.39 dex, from Hori et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2120 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.28651, from Hori et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
